# https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/neural_networks_supervised.html

import numpy as np
import util
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import time


def score(y_true, y_prob):
    """Weighted one-vs-rest ROC AUC, also handling the two class case."""
    y_prob = np.asarray(y_prob)
    if y_prob.ndim == 2 and y_prob.shape[1] == 2 and len(np.unique(np.asarray(y_true))) <= 2:
        return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob[:, 1], average="weighted")
    return roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob, multi_class="ovr", average="weighted")


def train_NN(filename, X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test, solver='adam', full_param=False, debug=False, numFolds=10,
             njobs=-1, scalar=1, make_graphs=False, pNN={}, nolegend=False):
    np.random.seed(1)
    algo = 'Neural Network'
    start = time.time()

    # A high max_iter with early stopping converges quickly without a wall of ConvergenceWarnings
    fixed_params = {'solver': solver, 'max_iter': 10000, 'early_stopping': True, 'random_state': 1}
    graph_name = str(filename)[:-4] + '-' + str(solver)  # keeps the adam and sgd figures apart

    if len(pNN) == 0:
        if full_param:
            param_grid = [{'hidden_layer_sizes': [(16,), (64,), (128,), (128, 128), (512, 512, 512, 512)],
                           'activation'        : ['relu', 'tanh'],  # 'identity', 'logistic'
                           'solver'            : [solver],
                           'alpha'             : [0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1],
                           'learning_rate_init': [0.001, 0.01],
                           'max_iter'          : [10000],
                           'early_stopping'    : [True],
                           'random_state'      : [1]
                           }]
        else:
            param_grid = [{'hidden_layer_sizes': [(16,), (64,)],
                           'activation'        : ['relu', 'tanh'],
                           'solver'            : [solver],
                           'alpha'             : [0.0001, 0.01],
                           'learning_rate_init': [0.01],
                           'max_iter'          : [10000],
                           'early_stopping'    : [True],
                           'random_state'      : [1]
                           }]

        nn_classifier = MLPClassifier(**fixed_params)

        grid_search = GridSearchCV(nn_classifier, param_grid, cv=numFolds,
                                   scoring='roc_auc_ovr_weighted',
                                   return_train_score=True, n_jobs=njobs, verbose=debug)
        grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
        cvres = grid_search.cv_results_
        best_params = dict(grid_search.best_params_)

        util.save_gridsearch_to_csv(cvres, algo, str(filename)[:-4], scalar, solver)

        if debug:
            print('Best Params:', best_params)
    else:
        best_params = dict(pNN)

    nn_classifier = MLPClassifier(**fixed_params)
    nn_classifier.set_params(**best_params)

    nn_classifier.fit(X_train, y_train)
    train_score = score(y_train, nn_classifier.predict_proba(X_train))
    test_score = score(y_test, nn_classifier.predict_proba(X_test))

    if make_graphs:
        # Learning curve plus the model complexity (validation) curves
        util.plot_learning_curve(nn_classifier, algo, graph_name, X_train, y_train, ylim=(0.0, 1.05),
                                 cv=numFolds, n_jobs=njobs, debug=debug)

        util.compute_vc(algo, 'alpha', [0.00001, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10],
                        X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, nn_classifier, graph_name,
                        MLPClassifier(**fixed_params), best_params, log=True, njobs=njobs, debug=debug,
                        nolegend=nolegend)

        util.compute_vc(algo, 'learning_rate_init', [0.00001, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1],
                        X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, nn_classifier, graph_name,
                        MLPClassifier(**fixed_params), best_params, log=True, njobs=njobs, debug=debug,
                        nolegend=nolegend)

        util.compute_vc(algo, 'hidden_layer_sizes', [(1,), (16,), (64,), (128,), (16, 16), (64, 64), (128, 128, 128)],
                        X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, nn_classifier, graph_name,
                        MLPClassifier(**fixed_params), best_params, njobs=njobs, debug=debug, fString=True,
                        rotatex=True, nolegend=nolegend)

        util.compute_vc(algo, 'activation', ['identity', 'logistic', 'tanh', 'relu'],
                        X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, nn_classifier, graph_name,
                        MLPClassifier(**fixed_params), best_params, njobs=njobs, debug=debug, fString=True,
                        nolegend=nolegend)

        # Loss of the fitted network, with the early stopping validation score when it was tracked
        loss_curve = getattr(nn_classifier, 'loss_curve_', None)
        if loss_curve:
            validation_scores = getattr(nn_classifier, 'validation_scores_', None)

            plt.figure()
            plt.grid()
            plt.title(algo + ' Loss Curve', fontsize=15)
            plt.xlabel("Iteration", fontsize=15)
            plt.ylabel("Loss", fontsize=15)
            plt.plot(np.arange(1, len(loss_curve) + 1), loss_curve, color='r', label="Training loss")

            if validation_scores:
                plt.plot(np.arange(1, len(validation_scores) + 1), validation_scores, color='g',
                         label="Validation score")

            if not nolegend:

import os

import numpy as np
from time import time

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.cm as cm

import pandas as pd

from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_samples, silhouette_score
from sklearn.cluster import MiniBatchKMeans, KMeans
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture
import copy
from yellowbrick.cluster import KElbowVisualizer

# All figures land in this folder, relative to the current working directory.
IMAGE_DIR = 'Images'


def save_figure(name):
    """Write the current figure into IMAGE_DIR, creating the folder when needed."""
    try:
        os.makedirs(IMAGE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(IMAGE_DIR, str(name).replace(os.sep, '-') + '.png'))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as err:  # never let a plot kill a run
        print('Unable to save figure', name, err)


def as_matrix(X):
    """Every pipeline accepts either a DataFrame or a plain ndarray."""
    if isinstance(X, (pd.DataFrame, pd.Series)):
        return X.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=float)


# Citation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_digits.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-cluster-plot-kmeans-digits-py
def bench_k_means(estimator, labels, name, data, sample_size, n_clusters, random_state, filename, verbose=False):
    t0 = time()
    estimator.fit(data)
    fit_time = time() - t0

    preds = estimator.predict(data)

    homo = metrics.homogeneity_score(labels, preds)
    comp = metrics.completeness_score(labels, preds)
    v_meas = metrics.v_measure_score(labels, preds)
    ari = metrics.adjusted_rand_score(labels, preds)
    ami = metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score(labels, preds)
    fks = metrics.fowlkes_mallows_score(labels, preds)
    silo = metrics.silhouette_score(data, preds, metric='euclidean', sample_size=sample_size,
                                    random_state=random_state)
    dbs = metrics.davies_bouldin_score(data, preds)
    chs = metrics.calinski_harabasz_score(data, preds)
    iner = estimator.inertia_
    if verbose:
        print('%-9s\t%d\t%.2fs\t%.2f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%.3f\t%i\t%i'
              % (name, n_clusters, fit_time, homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, iner)
              )

    return fit_time, homo, comp, v_meas, ari, ami, fks, silo, dbs, chs, iner


# Citation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_kmeans_silhouette_analysis.html#sphx-glr-auto-examples-cluster-plot-kmeans-silhouette-analysis-py
def silo_analysis(X, y, clusterer, n_clusters, random_state, filename):
    if filename == "Chess":
        col1, col2 = 0, 5
    else:
        col1, col2 = 13, 11

    X_m = as_matrix(X)
    # Reduced data can hold fewer columns than the two the write up plots
    col1, col2 = min(col1, X_m.shape[1] - 1), min(col2, X_m.shape[1] - 1)
    if col1 == col2:
        col1 = 0

    cluster_labels = clusterer.fit_predict(X_m)

    # The silhouette_score gives the average value for all the samples.
    # This gives a perspective into the density and separation of the formed
    # clusters
    silhouette_avg = silhouette_score(X_m, cluster_labels, metric='euclidean', sample_size=400,
                                      random_state=random_state)

    plt.figure()

    # The 1st subplot is the silhouette plot
    # The silhouette coefficient can range from -1, 1 but in this example all
    # lie within [-0.1, 1]
    plt.xlim([-0.1, 1])
    # The (n_clusters+1)*10 is for inserting blank space between silhouette
    # plots of individual clusters, to demarcate them clearly.
    plt.ylim([0, len(X_m) + (n_clusters + 1) * 10])

    # Compute the silhouette scores for each sample
    sample_silhouette_values = silhouette_samples(X_m, cluster_labels)

    y_lower = 10
    for i in range(n_clusters):
        # Aggregate the silhouette scores for samples belonging to
        # cluster i, and sort them
        ith_cluster_silhouette_values = \
            sample_silhouette_values[cluster_labels == i]

        ith_cluster_silhouette_values.sort()

        size_cluster_i = ith_cluster_silhouette_values.shape[0]
        y_upper = y_lower + size_cluster_i

        cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
        color = cmap(float(i) / n_clusters)
        plt.fill_betweenx(np.arange(y_lower, y_upper),
                          0, ith_cluster_silhouette_values,
                          facecolor=color, edgecolor=color, alpha=0.7)

        # Label the silhouette plots with their cluster numbers at the middle
        plt.text(-0.05, y_lower + 0.5 * size_cluster_i, str(i))

        # Compute the new y_lower for next plot
        y_lower = y_upper + 10  # 10 for the 0 samples

    plt.title("The silhouette plot for the various %d KMeans clusters." % n_clusters)

    plt.xlabel("The silhouette coefficient values")
    plt.ylabel("Cluster label")

    # The vertical line for average silhouette score of all the values
    plt.axvline(x=silhouette_avg, color="red", linestyle="--")

def init_analysis(X, y, n_clusters, filename):
    # Number of run (with randomly generated dataset) for each strategy so as
    # to be able to compute an estimate of the standard deviation
    n_runs = 5

    # k-means models can do several random inits so as to be able to trade
    # CPU time for convergence robustness
    n_init_range = np.array([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 50, 75, 100])

    # Part 1: Quantitative evaluation of various init methods

    plt.figure()
    plots = []
    legends = []

    cases = [
        (KMeans, 'k-means++', {}),
        (KMeans, 'random', {}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'k-means++', {'max_no_improvement': 3}),
        (MiniBatchKMeans, 'random', {'max_no_improvement': 3, 'init_size': 500}),
    ]

    for factory, init, params in cases:
        print("Evaluation of %s with %s init" % (factory.__name__, init))
        inertia = np.empty((len(n_init_range), n_runs))

        for run_id in range(n_runs):
            for i, n_init in enumerate(n_init_range):
                km = factory(n_clusters=n_clusters, init=init, random_state=run_id,
                             n_init=n_init, **params).fit(X)
                inertia[i, run_id] = km.inertia_
        p = plt.errorbar(n_init_range, inertia.mean(axis=1), inertia.std(axis=1))
        plots.append(p[0])
        legends.append("%s with %s init" % (factory.__name__, init))

    plt.xlabel('n_init')
    plt.ylabel('inertia')
    plt.legend(plots, legends)
    plt.title("Mean inertia for various k-means init across %d runs" % n_runs)
    save_figure(str(filename) + "Mean Interia across " + str(n_runs) + " runs and " + str(n_clusters) + " clusters")

    plt.close()

def init_analysis(X, y, n_clusters, filename):

    # to be able to compute an estimate of the standard deviation
    n_runs = 5

    # k-means models can do several random inits so as to be able to trade
    # CPU time for convergence robustness
    n_init_range = np.array([1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 50, 75, 100])

    plt.figure()
    plots = []
    legends = []

import os

import numpy as np
from sklearn import metrics

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


import pandas as pd
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA, FastICA
from sklearn.random_projection import GaussianRandomProjection as GRP
from itertools import product
from collections import defaultdict
from sklearn.manifold import LocallyLinearEmbedding
from scipy.stats import kurtosis

# All figures land in this folder, relative to the current working directory.
IMAGE_DIR = 'Images'


def save_figure(name):
    """Write the current figure into IMAGE_DIR, creating the folder when needed."""
    try:
        os.makedirs(IMAGE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(IMAGE_DIR, str(name).replace(os.sep, '-') + '.png'))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as err:  # never let a plot kill a run
        print('Unable to save figure', name, err)


def as_matrix(X):
    """Every pipeline accepts either a DataFrame or a plain ndarray."""
    if isinstance(X, (pd.DataFrame, pd.Series)):
        return X.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=float)


def ulPCA(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    X_m = as_matrix(X)
    n_samples, n_features = X_m.shape

    pca = PCA(svd_solver='full', random_state=random_seed)
    pca.fit(X_m)

    eigenvalues = pca.explained_variance_
    variance_ratio = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
    cumulative = np.cumsum(variance_ratio)
    n_components = [i for i in range(1, len(variance_ratio) + 1)]

    if verbose:
        print("PCA - n_samples %d, \t n_features %d, \t n_components %d"
              % (n_samples, n_features, len(n_components)))
        print('n\teigenvalue\tvariance\tcumulative')
        for n, eig, var, cum in zip(n_components, eigenvalues, variance_ratio, cumulative):
            print('%d\t%.6f\t%.6f\t%.6f' % (n, eig, var, cum))

    # Per component variance on the left axis, the cumulative curve on the right
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots()
    plt.title("PCA Explained Variance - " + str(filename), fontsize=16)
    ax1.bar(n_components, variance_ratio, color='blue', alpha=0.6, label='Per Component')
    ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Components', fontsize=16)
    ax1.set_ylabel('Explained Variance Ratio', color='blue', fontsize=16)
    ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='blue', labelsize=16)
    ax1.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=16)
    ax1.legend(prop={'size': 12}, loc='center right')

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    color = 'tab:red'
    ax2.set_ylabel('Cumulative Explained Variance', color=color, fontsize=16)
    ax2.plot(n_components, cumulative, 'o-', color=color, label='Cumulative')
    ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color, labelsize=16)
    ax2.legend(prop={'size': 12}, loc='lower right')
    fig.tight_layout()
    save_figure(str(filename) + '-PCA-Explained-Variance')
    plt.close(fig)

    # Scree plot of the eigenvalues, the classic elbow for picking components
    plt.figure()
    plt.plot(n_components, eigenvalues, 'o-')
    plt.title("PCA Eigenvalues - " + str(filename), fontsize=16)
    plt.xlabel('Number of Components', fontsize=16)
    plt.ylabel('Eigenvalue', fontsize=16)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.xticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.yticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.tight_layout()
    save_figure(str(filename) + '-PCA-Eigenvalues')
    plt.close()


def ulICA(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    X_m = as_matrix(X)
    n_samples, n_features = X_m.shape

    dims = [i for i in range(1, min(n_features, n_samples) + 1)]

    mean_kurt_arr, max_kurt_arr, recon_arr = [], [], []

    if verbose:
        print("ICA - n_samples %d, \t n_features %d" % (n_samples, n_features))
        print('n\tmean kurt\tmax kurt\trecon error')

    for dim in dims:
        ica = FastICA(n_components=dim, random_state=random_seed)
        try:
            components = ica.fit_transform(X_m)
            # Kurtosis is the ICA signal, non gaussian components carry the information
            kurt = np.abs(kurtosis(components, axis=0, fisher=True))
            mean_kurt = float(np.nanmean(kurt))
            max_kurt = float(np.nanmax(kurt))
            recon = metrics.mean_squared_error(X_m, ica.inverse_transform(components))
        except Exception as err:  # a component count that will not converge should not stop the sweep
            print('Unable to fit ICA with n_components =', dim, ':', err)
            mean_kurt, max_kurt, recon = np.nan, np.nan, np.nan

        mean_kurt_arr.append(mean_kurt)
        max_kurt_arr.append(max_kurt)
        recon_arr.append(recon)

        if verbose:
            print('%d\t%.6f\t%.6f\t%.6f' % (dim, mean_kurt, max_kurt, recon))

    # Kurtosis by number of components
    plt.figure()
    plt.plot(dims, mean_kurt_arr, 'o-', label='Mean |Kurtosis|')
    plt.plot(dims, max_kurt_arr, 'o-', label='Max |Kurtosis|')
    plt.title("ICA Kurtosis - " + str(filename), fontsize=16)
    plt.xlabel('Number of Components', fontsize=16)
    plt.ylabel('Absolute Kurtosis', fontsize=16)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.xticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.yticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.legend(prop={'size': 12})
    plt.tight_layout()
    save_figure(str(filename) + '-ICA-Kurtosis')
    plt.close()

    # Reconstruction error of the inverse transform
    plt.figure()
    plt.plot(dims, recon_arr, 'o-')
    plt.title("ICA Reconstruction Error - " + str(filename), fontsize=16)
    plt.xlabel('Number of Components', fontsize=16)
    plt.ylabel('Mean Squared Error', fontsize=16)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.xticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.yticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.tight_layout()
    save_figure(str(filename) + '-ICA-Reconstruction-Error')
    plt.close()


def randProj(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    X_m = as_matrix(X)
    n_samples, n_features = X_m.shape

    dims = [i for i in range(1, n_features + 1)]
    seeds = [random_seed + i for i in range(5)]

    # Random projections vary with the seed, so every dimension is run several times
    errors = defaultdict(dict)
    for dim, seed in product(dims, seeds):
        rp = GRP(n_components=dim, random_state=seed)
        projected = rp.fit_transform(X_m)
        # GRP has no inverse_transform, unproject with the pseudo inverse of the projection
        reconstructed = projected.dot(np.linalg.pinv(rp.components_).T)
        errors[dim][seed] = metrics.mean_squared_error(X_m, reconstructed)

    recon_df = pd.DataFrame(errors)
    recon_mean = recon_df.mean(axis=0).to_numpy()
    recon_std = recon_df.std(axis=0).to_numpy()

    if verbose:
        print("RP - n_samples %d, \t n_features %d, \t n_seeds %d" % (n_samples, n_features, len(seeds)))
        print('n\tmean recon error\tstd')
        for dim, mean, std in zip(dims, recon_mean, recon_std):
            print('%d\t%.6f\t%.6f' % (dim, mean, std))

    plt.figure()
    plt.errorbar(dims, recon_mean, yerr=recon_std, fmt='o-', capsize=3, label='Mean +/- Std')
    plt.fill_between(dims, recon_mean - recon_std, recon_mean + recon_std, alpha=0.2)
    plt.title("RP Reconstruction Error - " + str(filename), fontsize=16)
    plt.xlabel('Number of Components', fontsize=16)
    plt.ylabel('Mean Squared Error', fontsize=16)
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.xticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.yticks(fontsize=16)
    plt.legend(prop={'size': 12})
    plt.tight_layout()
    save_figure(str(filename) + '-RP-Reconstruction-Error')
    plt.close()


def ul_LLE(X, y, random_seed, filename, verbose=False):
    X_m = as_matrix(X)
    n_samples, n_features = X_m.shape

    n_neighbors = 10
    # LLE is the slow technique here, keep the sweep bounded by the feature count
    max_dim = min(n_features, n_samples - 1)
    dims = [i for i in range(1, max_dim + 1)]

    recon_arr = []

    if verbose:
        print("LLE - n_samples %d, \t n_features %d, \t n_neighbors %d" % (n_samples, n_features, n_neighbors))
        print('n\trecon error')

    for dim in dims:
        lle = LocallyLinearEmbedding(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, n_components=dim, random_state=random_seed, n_jobs=-1)
        try:
            lle.fit(X_m)
            recon = lle.reconstruction_error_
        except Exception as err:  # some component counts are degenerate, keep the sweep going
            print('Unable to fit LLE with n_components =', dim, ':', err)
            recon = np.nan

        recon_arr.append(recon)

        if verbose:
            print('%d\t%.8f' % (dim, recon))

    plt.figure()
